shortlist.label: Sézary syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: skin lesions, lymphadenopathy not noted but lymphocytes with atypical CD3-negative, CD4-negative, CD5-positive, CD8-positive phenotype, and clonal rearrangements identified in skin biopsy and bone marrow samples

raw.rationale: The presence of dermal papules, nodular to diffuse lymphohistiocytic infiltrate, and atypical lymphocytes with numerous histiocytes on skin biopsy, along with clonal rearrangements identified in skin biopsy and bone marrow samples, are characteristic of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. The patient's symptoms and biopsy results are more consistent with this diagnosis than Sézary syndrome, which typically presents with more widespread skin involvement, lymphadenopathy, and a higher burden of circulating malignant cells.

rejected.label: Sézary syndrome
rejected.why: The patient lacks the typical features of Sézary syndrome, such as widespread skin erythroderma, lymphadenopathy, and a high burden of circulating malignant cells. The presence of dermal papules and the specific immunophenotypic profile of the lymphocytes are more consistent with cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
